## History of the Old and New Testaments.

**Chronology** <note>original: "Tydrékening"</note> is the science of the times in which events occurred.

This knowledge is absolutely necessary to have a clear idea of the histories and deeds with which the memory is enriched when reading histories; without it, everything is confused and obscure, and one does not have half the pleasure and benefit that is otherwise found in that reading.

It is true that it is not always easy to know the order of time well, and to put every matter in its right place: The Assyrians, the Chaldeans, and the Egyptians, who since the Flood are the oldest nations of the world, can give us no help in this today. In olden times people wrote few books; those which may have been written in those remote <note>original: "achterlyke," here meaning distant or early</note> times have not come to our knowledge, and the fragments of some, less ancient, preserved in the authors—whom one could call "new" in respect to that first antiquity—are more suited to give birth to difficulties than to give great light to the ignorance in which one finds oneself regarding ancient History and Chronology.

The Greeks came later and have written much. But besides the fact that the best and oldest of their books have been lost through the upheavals of times and nations, they have mixed their stories with so many fables that almost no reliance can be placed on what they tell us of those first times, which preceded the siege of Troy, and for that reason are commonly called the fabulous times.

The oldest of all books in the world is, without contradiction, the Holy Scripture. Moses lived more than four hundred years before Homer; and Homer is the oldest of the Greek writers.

The history of Moses begins with the Creation. It is certain that the world is not eternal: one needs only a small amount of knowledge and a little reflection to be convinced of this. The Pagans <note>original: "Heydenen," referring to the non-Christian/Jewish peoples of antiquity</note> believed this as well as we, and some even of their poets and philosophers made a description of the Creation which looks quite a bit like that which Moses has given us. Yet it is from him alone that one can learn how long ago the world was created.

He has made a Chronology of it, by setting down the lineage of the first men and pointing out to us how many years they lived. The lives of men in those first times were very long, in comparison with what it was since, and still is today. A man of a hundred years is nowadays considered very old: but formerly those were but as the years of childhood; a person lived seven or eight hundred years: yet no one ever reached a thousand; but several came close to it. Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years; and Methuselah nine hundred and sixty-nine. One must not imagine that such a vast difference between the lives of the people of then and of our time arises from a different manner of calculating the years, as if our years were much longer than theirs. This is nothing but a mere imagination. All the years of which the Holy Scripture speaks were of twelve months, and each month of twenty-nine days: for the calculation of the beginning of the months was according to the cycle of the Moon, as being much more apparent and easier to notice than that of the Sun. One only needs to read the history of the Flood to have no doubt about this.

It is in everyone's choice to make such a division of the time of the world as he wishes, and to divide it into three, into four, or into six, or more great periods <term>tydbeſtekken<gloss>significant spans or eras of time</gloss></term>, as he sees fit. For such divisions are only invented to come to the aid of memory; and whatever one calls it, everything eventually comes to the same result.

<summary>This page introduces the concept of Chronology as an essential science for understanding Biblical history, asserting that Holy Scripture is the oldest and most reliable record of time compared to ancient secular sources.</summary>
<keywords>Chronology, Holy Scripture, Moses, Creation, Methuselah, longevity of patriarchs, lunar calendar, ancient historians</keywords>

# OF HOLY SCRIPTURE.

The most common practice is to divide all the time that has elapsed since the Creation of the world until Jesus Christ into six periods, or six ages, each of which begins with a remarkable event well-suited to be impressed upon the memory. Each beginning of these divisions is called by the general name of *Epoch* or **Time-root** <note>original: "Tydwortel"</note>, which in Chronology or History is a kind of fixed point and a certain time from which one begins to count the years.

The **first age** begins with the Creation and ends with the Flood, being 1,656 years.

The **second** is from the Flood, or the departure of Noah and his family from the ark—in which they had been enclosed for a year—until the calling of Abraham, occurring in the year of the world 2083, and thus comprises 426 years.

The **third age** is from the calling of Abraham until the departure from Egypt, and contains 430 years.

The **fourth** is from the exodus from Egypt until the founding of Solomon’s Temple, which makes about 480 years.

The **fifth**, from the founding of the Temple until the end of the Babylonian captivity, and includes 476 years within it.

The **sixth** is from the end of the seventy years of the Babylonian captivity—which was the time when Cyrus granted the Jews freedom to settle again in their Fatherland and to rebuild Jerusalem and the Temple—until the birth of our Savior Jesus Christ; and that age or cycle of time was 532 years, provided one places the birth of Christ in the year four thousand after the Creation of the world, as the most accurate Chronologists do; namely, four years earlier than the common Chronology, which places the same four years later, in the year of Creation 4004. <note>This refers to the famous "Ussher chronology," which traditionally dated creation to 4004 BC. The author notes a slight scholarly disagreement of four years but dismisses it as insignificant over such a long span.</note> But this difference is of no importance in such a large number of years.

These first six ages of the world are followed by a **seventh**, which crowns all the others, being the longest of all, and which alone has brought more happiness to earth than all the other six combined; this is the period in which we live, and which is specifically that of the Christian Church. It took its beginning with the birth of Jesus Christ and must last until the end of the world.

Since our intention is not to fill this chronological sketch with a multitude of deeds that are either little known or of little necessity—better suited to satisfy curiosity than to serve the understanding of holy History—we shall keep to the Chronology contained in the books of the Old Testament, just as it has pleased God to preserve them for our instruction in their original language, which is Hebrew. For regarding the Greek Bible of the **LXX Translators** <note>original: "LXX. Overzetteren," referring to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note>, who greatly increased the count of the years of the Patriarchs, we shall take no notice of it at all. It is not safe to follow guides who have so often deviated from the Hebrew Text in their translation; and since they have taken the liberty to change many things in various places of the Scripture according to their pleasure, and since all others deviate from them therein, we consider ourselves not bound to follow them in a chronology that differs so much from the original Hebrew.

But to make this sketch as short and at the same time as easy as possible, we shall follow the order and arrangement of the learned **Usserius** <note>James Ussher (1581–1656), Archbishop of Armagh, whose biblical timeline became the standard for centuries</note>, Archbishop of Armagh in Ireland, because we see that the most accurate Chronologists of various religions who have written after him have followed the same. And without binding ourselves to everything, whether of his designs or thoughts, we shall, as he has done, contain in short Tables the years of the Patriarchs, the Judges, and the Kings of God's people; in order to show the reader at a single glance what we could not explain in a discourse without much long-windedness.

From this Chronological Table, it appears that Noah, who is the last listed upon it and constitutes the tenth generation, could have seen people from seven generations before him, all of whom had seen Adam; thus, he could have received from them the knowledge of the matters which Moses relates in the opening chapters of his first Book <note>The Book of Genesis</note>.

Methuselah, the grandfather of Noah, could have lived 246 years with Adam, and nearly six hundred years with his grandson Noah. Thus, it was an easy matter for the history of the Creation to be preserved entirely, and for the faith in the promise of the Messiah—contained in the words of God to Adam in Genesis 3:15: *The seed of the Woman shall bruise the head of the Serpent, etc.* <note>original: "Het zaad der Vrouwe zal den kop der Slange vermorzelen, enz."</note>—to pass from father to son within the households of the believers.

Note that the author acknowledges a discrepancy in dating systems, specifically regarding the year of Christ's birth (4000 AM vs. 4004 AM).</meta>

OF HOLY SCRIPTURE.

### The Sixth Age of the World.

The sixth age of the world begins with the return from the Babylonian captivity, in the year 3468; and ends with the birth of Jesus Christ, in the year 4000, thus encompassing a span of 532 years. During that time, Judea was subject to the Persians, descendants of Cyrus, for about 200 years; to Alexander, conqueror of Darius (the last King of the Persians), or to the Seleucids, Kings of Syria, for about 180 years; and finally to the Romans, after the city of Jerusalem was taken by Pompey, 65 years before the birth of Jesus Christ. Consequently, the Jews were not entirely free and independent of foreign powers from the time of their return from the captivity of Babylon, except for about 70 or 80 years.

---
<image-desc>Decorative horizontal divider consisting of a row of ornate floral fleurons.</image-desc>

### The Seventh Age of the World.

The seventh and final age of the world began with the birth of our Savior, and shall not end until the world itself ends.

Common opinion places, as we have said before, the birth of Christ in the year 4004. However, the most accurate chronologists <note>Original: "Tydrékenaars," referring to scholars who calculate historical dates and timelines.</note> move it forward by 4 years and place it in the year of the world 4000. Nevertheless, in this entire History, we have followed the common method of calculating the years to avoid confusion with the chronologies that are already in everyone's hands.

The birth of John the Baptist occurred only six months before that of Jesus Christ; and our Savior received baptism from him in the 30th year of his age, and died in the middle of his 33rd year.

Three days later he rose again; on the 40th day after his death, he ascended into Heaven; and on the 50th, which was Pentecost <note>Original: "Pingsterdag," the Christian festival celebrating the descent of the Holy Spirit.</note>, he sent the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles gathered in Jerusalem. And this guilty city <note>The author uses "misdaadige stad" (criminal/guilty city), reflecting a common historical theological view regarding the rejection of Christ by the leadership in Jerusalem.</note> perished along with the Temple and the entire Jewish State 37 years after the death of Jesus Christ, being the 70th year after his birth.

We thus pass briefly over everything because these things are so well known that it would be unnecessary to speak of them at length in a simple sketch such as this is.

---
<image-desc>Decorative horizontal divider consisting of a row of ornate floral fleurons.</image-desc>

## Regarding the Time in Which the Most Renowned Prophets of the Ancient Jewish People Lived.

The Prophets played too great a part in the governance of God’s people to be forgotten in this brief summary of sacred chronology. It may have its use in various matters, and especially when one considers the prophecies with regard to the time of their fulfillment under the new Dispensation <note>Original: "Bedelinge," a theological term for the different ways or eras in which God deals with humanity.</note>.

The Prophets, then, were extraordinary men to whom God revealed himself immediately, and whom he filled with his Spirit—sometimes to powerfully rebuke the Jews for their crimes and to rekindle the zeal that was almost extinguished in the Church; sometimes to present his oracles to the Kings who ruled over his people, and to foretell the good or evil that was destined for them. These were the most tangible duties of their service, but the primary one was to foretell the Messiah and to point him out through so many passages and identifying marks that would be unique to him, so that the Church—for which alone God prepared such a great gift for the earth—could not be ignorant of him when God would send him into the world. The entire ancient Dispensation was directed toward that, and for that reason, one finds the Messiah in almost all the writings of the Prophets, and one perceives in the greatest part of their oracles that happy dispensation of grace and peace which we call the Gospel.

The first and most renowned of all the Prophets is Moses, who was a prophet and redeemer of God’s people, and at the same time a Mediator of the covenant between the Lord and his people. God appeared to him on Mount Horeb in a miraculous flame that burned in a bramble bush without consuming it. After that time, Moses was enlightened by the spirit of prophecy until his death, which occurred forty years later.
